title: Accelerating Multi-Scalar Multiplication for Efficient Zero Knowledge Proofs with Multi-GPU Systems
problem: Multi-Scalar Multiplication (MSM) accounts for 78.2% of zero-knowledge proof generation workload, and even with GPU acceleration, proof generation takes minutes. MSM computation becomes the critical bottleneck limiting ZKP scalability and adoption.
motivation: Zero-knowledge proofs enable verifiable outsourcing and digital currency, but widespread adoption is limited by the extensive time required for proof generation.
method: DistMSM adapts Pippenger's algorithm for distributed multi-GPU systems, identifying and resolving bottlenecks at scale. At the GPU kernel level, it introduces an optimized elliptic curve arithmetic kernel that reduces register pressure via two novel techniques and leverages tensor cores for efficient big integer multiplication.
key_novelty: Multi-GPU adapted Pippenger's algorithm with bottleneck-aware optimization and specialized elliptic curve kernel for distributed proof acceleration.
contributions: DistMSM algorithm tailored for distributed multi-GPU systems
Pippenger's algorithm adaptation addressing multi-GPU scaling bottlenecks
Optimized elliptic curve arithmetic kernel with register pressure reduction
Tensor core utilization for big integer multiplications

metrics.speedup: 6.39x average across elliptic curves and GPU counts
metrics.other: Latency reduction from seconds to tens of milliseconds per MSM task

primary_theme: Multi-GPU distributed acceleration for zero-knowledge proofs
